# W3 — Resize the Gerrit host t4g.large -> r7g.large (2 vCPU, 8 GiB -> 2 vCPU, 16 GiB)

Implements workstream **W3** of parent epic `couped-subzero-wolf` ("Right-size or change
instance family"), which that epic records as an **operator decision because it costs money**.
The operator has approved r7g.large and **capped the change at r7g.large's cost**; larger
types are out of scope by that approval.

## Context / Problem

The sibling story `cryptozoic-unlit-ladybug` (the $0 half) sizes four per-service container
memory limits from measured steady state. Those limits do not fit the current host:

```
gerrit 3072 + mcp 3655 + review-bot 1343 + opcert 256  =  9088 MiB
host total (measured `free -m`, 2026-09-06 01:29 UTC)  =  7813 MiB   -> OVER by 1275 MiB
```

MCP alone measures **2.87 GiB** steady state (post-change-2685, recorded on the epic under
AC6) — 38% of the present box. The $0 half is therefore arithmetically unlandable as sized:
either a service shrinks below measured demand, or the host grows. This grows the host to
16 GiB, leaving the 9,088 MiB limit sum roughly 42% headroom on a 16,384 MiB machine.

## Why r7g.large, and why vCPU deliberately does NOT change

| type | vCPU | MiB | on-demand/mo | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| t4g.large (current) | 2 | 8192 | $49.06 | memory-starved |
| **r7g.large** | 2 | 16384 | $78.18 | **approved ceiling** |
| c7g.xlarge | 4 | 8192 | $105.85 | over approval; does not fix memory |
| m7g.xlarge | 4 | 16384 | $119.14 | over approval |

The binding constraint is **memory, not CPU**. The peak load average of 5.08 on the epic was
measured while six heavyweight consumers ran concurrently (three `make verify` runs plus three
`review-plan` gates) against a 4-slot semaphore — unbounded concurrency, which
`cryptozoic-unlit-ladybug` separately fixes, not steady demand. Sustained demand measured
~1.1 vCPU; current load 0.74. So vCPU holds at 2 and this buys only RAM. Any case for more
vCPU is a separate ticket and the operator's cost decision.

r7g is additionally **not burstable**, which relieves the concern in
`relevant-dissident-salamander` (t4g credits pinned at zero since 12:38Z, on billed surplus):
a non-burstable family has no credit balance to exhaust. That is a side effect, not the
justification, and does not close that bug.

## Why this is AMI-compatible (the risk that would break the host)

`infra/terraform/main.tf:12-14` resolves the AMI from the public SSM parameter
`/aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-arm64` — an **arm64** image —
pinned by `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [ami] }` at `main.tf:96-98`. A non-arm64 instance type
would produce an instance that cannot boot. r7g is Graviton3 (arm64), so the swap preserves
architecture. AC2 requires that be **verified against the API**, not asserted from the name.

## What changes

One default plus the description documenting its constraint:

- `infra/terraform/variables.tf:7-11` — `variable "instance_type"` default `"t4g.large"` ->
  `"r7g.large"`, with the description's Graviton/arm64 sentence retargeted to the type that is
  actually configured.

No resource edits: `aws_instance.gerrit` (`main.tf:67-104`) already reads `var.instance_type`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 `infra/terraform/variables.tf` declares `instance_type` default `"r7g.large"` and
      its `description` states the arm64/Graviton constraint in terms of `r7g.large`. Verified
      by `grep -c 't4g' infra/terraform/variables.tf` returning 0 and `grep -n 'r7g.large'`
      returning both the default line and the description line.
- [ ] AC2 r7g.large is proven arm64 and offered in the instance's AZ **from the AWS API**, and
      the AMI the config selects is proven arm64. Verified by
      `aws ec2 describe-instance-types --instance-types r7g.large`,
      `aws ec2 describe-instance-type-offerings` filtered to `us-east-1a`, and
      `aws ec2 describe-images` on the id the SSM parameter resolves to. Transcript recorded
      as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] AC3 `terraform plan` GENERATES (exit 0 or 2, never 1, no `Error:` line) and shows
      `aws_instance.gerrit` **`will be updated in-place`**, **`0 to destroy`**, and no
      `forces replacement` / `must be replaced` anywhere. An instance-type change on an
      EBS-backed instance is stop/modify/start, not replacement; a plan saying otherwise means
      STOP, because a replacement would destroy the Gerrit host. Transcript recorded on this
      ticket.
- [ ] AC4 The pre-existing unapplied drift the plan carries is enumerated in a comment on this
      ticket so the Phase-2 apply is not a surprise. This ticket does not reconcile it.
- [ ] AC5 A sweep for an existing infra-invariant test covering instance sizing is recorded
      (`grep -rn 't4g|instance_type' tests/`): if one exists it is updated; if none exists,
      that is stated rather than a new test invented. `make verify` passes.
- [ ] AC6 The change lands through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`. The apply is
      NOT part of this change — it is a separate operator-authorised step after the merge.

## Apply plan (Phase 2, operator-gated: recorded so it is reviewable, not executed here)

1. EBS snapshots of both attached volumes (root + gerrit data), ids recorded on this ticket,
   BEFORE the apply.
2. `terraform apply`. This **stops and starts the instance**: expect a Gerrit outage of ~3
   minutes (a prior stop/start on this host ran 23:51:25 -> 23:54:17). Expected, not a fault.
3. Post-apply verification, recorded on this ticket:
   - all four containers healthy (`gerrit`, `mcp`, `review-bot`, `opcert`). Watch
     **review-bot**: containers use `unless-stopped`, and one that `Exited (0)` does NOT
     restart across a host stop/start — that silently removed the `LLM-Review` vote source for
     59 minutes earlier this session, the failure `complex-sassy-blackfly` records.
   - `free -m` reports ~16 GiB total.
   - the gate-scratch volume is still mounted at `var.gate_scratch_mount`. It is fstab-by-UUID
     with `nofail`, and `nofail` is exactly what permits a silent fallback to the root
     filesystem. Verified with `mountpoint -q` + `findmnt`, and by confirming the two markers
     sit on DIFFERENT devices (`stat -c %d` on `/var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required` vs
     `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted`), the check `injurious-wellmade-moth`
     established.
   - Gerrit answers HTTP 200 and `git ls-remote` succeeds.
   - no NEW CloudWatch alarms attributable to the resize.

## Risks

- **Replacement instead of in-place modify** — destroys the host. Caught by AC3 before apply.
- **Architecture mismatch** — unbootable instance. Caught by AC2 before push.
- **Gate-scratch not remounting** — silently undoes `injurious-wellmade-moth`. Caught by the
  two-marker different-device check.
- **review-bot not restarting** — silently removes the `LLM-Review` gate. Explicitly checked.
- **Cost** — +$29.12/mo. The approved figure and the approved ceiling.

## Not in scope

Types above r7g.large's cost; the container limits themselves (`cryptozoic-unlit-ladybug`);
reconciling the pre-existing terraform drift; closing `relevant-dissident-salamander`.
